what_happened: Re-measured the suite-selection-lib.sh header's carried '0 of 19 non-core suites match the deployed-vs-source hazard' figure directly against the 25 real non-core suites (approvals/books/lean/literature/typst). 5 of 25 (test-approve-classify.sh, test-approve-paths.sh, test-approve-refusals.sh, test-approve-structural.sh, test-lean-mcp-preflight-check.sh) carry at least one $REPO_ROOT/.claude or /.claude/ reference, so the frozen 0-of-19 figure does not hold under direct re-measurement; it was also almost certainly an artifact of suite_selection_classify's suite-file lookup being core-tree-only, which silently falls back to its vacuous 'source-only' default for any non-core suite basename it cannot locate from the source store -- not a genuine absence of the hazard. Recommended the classification axis be extended alongside the selection-mapping fix and the figure re-derived fresh post-fix rather than carried forward again.

The research report named the root cause (one-time root derivation consumed by all three strata), the reuse idiom (run-all.sh's core/manifest.json marker check), and the classification ruling with its own re-measurement, so planning needed only live confirmation (suite_selection_select on the lean path returned __FULL_SWEEP__ exactly as described) rather than re-derivation.

First draft of the plan named the bare shellcheck binary in three phase verification criteria instead of the repository's sanctioned entry point lint/lint-shellcheck.sh, which plan-format-enforcement.md forbids; corrected before writing final metadata, and validate-artifact.sh then passed with 0 warnings.

Phase 1 verification step's literal prediction for the core-path suite_selection_select invocation (a single suite, test-run-all-selection.sh) did not hold either before or after the edit: the unedited library already returned three suites for that path via the pre-existing stratum-(b) grep reference (two other suites genuinely reference the filename in their own source). This does not affect correctness -- output is byte-identical before/after the Phase 1 edit, which is the actual no-narrowing evidence -- but the plan's worked example was imprecise.

Fixed suite-selection-lib.sh's non-core-extension-path blind spot: a touched path under any extension's scripts/ now resolves to that extension's own paired suite instead of falsely escalating to __FULL_SWEEP__ (confirmed live: the lean path in the originating incident now resolves to test-lean-challenge-snapshot.sh). Extended suite_selection_classify to reach non-core suites via a shared marker-check helper, and re-measured the carried 0-of-19 figure: live corpus is 29 non-core suites, 9 of which (5 source-first, 4 deployed-first) actually carry the deployed-vs-source hazard, directly contradicting the stale claim. Four new pinning cases added and each independently confirmed load-bearing by reverting the corresponding code and observing the matching case fail. Suite passes from both source-store (36/0) and deployed (32/0, 4 cases cleanly skip where no extensions root exists) vantage points. Deploy-headless.sh's own embedded verify-deploy.sh run also passed clean (43 checks, 0 failures) as a side effect of the redeploy step.
